phases.none: No hosted operation (public landing page, composed titles, offline editing).
phases.A: Phase A: ONE analyst login, then authenticated read-only pages. Needs separate approval and R1 confirmation.
phases.B: Phase B: bounded simulator traffic and exactly one incident. Needs separate approval.
phases.C: Phase C: exactly one Gemini request behind a browser-level guard. Needs separate approval.

scenes.title: Opening and product identity
scenes.source: Hyperframes title sequence (no app footage, no fabricated UI)

scenes.title: Platform landing page
scenes.notes: The animated map on the landing and login pages uses the frontend's bundled DEMO data (utils/demoSources.js), not real attackers: captions must not imply otherwise.

captions.label: PLATFORM
lines: From raw logs to a live security picture.

captions.label: PLATFORM
lines: One console for the analyst workflow.

scenes.title: Authentication (the ONE login)
scenes.notes: The single analyst login. Saves the browser session to .auth/state.json for every later scene. Password is a masked field and is never revealed; no --auth-setup, no second login.

captions.label: ACCESS
lines: Signing in as a SOC analyst.

scenes.title: SOC dashboard
scenes.notes: Map geolocation is a deterministic placeholder (24 cities): never describe attacker locations as accurate. 'Alerts by severity' and 'Alert volume' live here, not on /analytics.

captions.label: DASHBOARD
lines: Tracking alerts, activity and emerging threats.

captions.label: DASHBOARD
lines: Attack origins on the threat map.

scenes.title: Security events table
scenes.notes: Filters and drawer are GET-only. NEVER press 'Explain & next steps' (Gemini).

captions.label: EVENTS
lines: Each row carries its detection result.

captions.label: EVENTS
lines: Raw log, normalised fields and model scores.

scenes.title: Live event stream
scenes.notes: The page shows only WebSocket events received while open. Without authorised simulator traffic it is empty; the 'live' caption is emitted ONLY if rows actually appear, otherwise a neutral standby caption.

scenes.title: Alert investigation
scenes.notes: Rows are table rows (click the row, never a chip). Filters are read-only. NEVER use Status, Assign, Comment, Open incident or 'Explain with AI' here.

scenes.title: Incident management
scenes.notes: Creates EXACTLY ONE incident from one approved alert, records its UUID, then makes ONE status change on that UUID. No response-action or approval screens exist in the UI and none are shown.

captions.label: INCIDENT
lines: Linking it to the investigated alert.

scenes.title: Attack path and kill chain
scenes.notes: Uses existing data in the selected window. Richer after Phase B traffic, but Phase A is enough to record it.

captions.label: ATTACK PATH
lines: Understanding the progression of an attack.

scenes.title: Threat intelligence
scenes.notes: Lookup is a GET. NEVER use the 'Add indicator' form. The indicator looked up is read from the first row of the existing list, not invented.

captions.label: THREAT INTELLIGENCE
lines: Checking an indicator against the feed.

scenes.title: Analytics
scenes.notes: /analytics shows alert and event volume trends only. Severity breakdown is on the dashboard.

scenes.title: ML models
scenes.notes: No accuracy claims beyond what the page displays (UNSW-NB15 held-out split). The PNG download is a client-side file; it modifies no application data.

scenes.title: Assistant (view only)
scenes.notes: View only. NEVER click a suggestion chip (each sends a Gemini request immediately).

scenes.title: Assistant (one approved request)
scenes.notes: Exactly one POST /assistant/analyze, enforced by the browser guard. Skip the scene if the answer is the [OFFLINE MODE] fallback. Never use suggestion chips.

captions.label: ASSISTANT
lines: Asking for a summary of recent alerts.

scenes.title: User administration (admin, view only)
scenes.notes: Admin account only. View only: NEVER use the New user form, the role selects or Deactivate. Name and email cells are blurred in the composition.

captions.label: ADMINISTRATION
lines: Administration is limited to the admin role.

scenes.title: Profile and settings
scenes.notes: Recorded as the admin account against the LOCAL stack. Profile/Settings show the account email and API URL: those rows are blurred in the composition. NEVER press Sign out, Update password or 'Detect again' (IP lookup).

captions.label: ACCOUNT
lines: Identifiers are masked in this film.

captions.label: ACCOUNT
lines: Live updates and loaded detection models.

scenes.title: Closing
scenes.source: Last frames of the 04-dashboard recording under a Hyperframes title
